races.name: Alan Rae Smith Errant Novice Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Oneinthewell
runners_data.note: All turf form over 20f+ on Good/Soft surfaces is a significant concern on Standard AW Polytrack over 1m4f — the going tag flags a legitimate worry — but James Owen's handler angle and the hold-up style suit a scenario where one lone leader sets a comfortable tempo; confidence in her winning remains low.

runners_data.name: Affettuoso
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 3yo shows a clear front-running tendency and has one AW placing (2nd, 10f, Standard) to her name, giving her course-surface relevance; 95 days off the track and a STYLE_FIT flag remind us she is racing out of optimal role if she can't dictate, but in a 5-runner field with no rival to trouble her early, she is likely to get exactly what she wants.

runners_data.name: Electric Arc
runners_data.note: George Boughey's 3yo has a single AW start — an eighth at 12f on Standard — and carries a flag for fading in the finish, which is a serious concern at this trip; Pat Cosgrave gives her experienced handling but it is hard to construct a winning scenario when her one relevant run saw her beaten and stopping.

runners_data.name: Astrid
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard flags her as a key danger, and two AW runs on Standard going (including a 3rd over 10f) give her legitimate course-surface credentials; Connor Beasley rides from the hold-up position and the extended trip over 1m4f looks an opportunity to test her stamina at novice level.

runners_data.name: Lost In Wonder
runners_data.note: A long 131 days off the track, a moderate OR of 59, and a form string showing repeated low finishes (7-2-5-7-8) make her hard to fancy despite the prominent style that sees her track whatever gallop Affettuoso sets; Camilla Poulton's yard shows no 14-day runners recorded, adding a stable-form concern.

races.paceDynamic: Affettuoso is the race's sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Lost In Wonder showing any prominent tendencies to potentially push forward, she should secure an uncontested lead into the first bend at Lingfield's 1m4f trip. With no serious challenger to her early position, she can dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop around the sweeping left-handed track, which at Standard Polytrack typically rewards horses that travel smoothly in midfield or just off the pace before delivering a measured late run. Oneinthewell and Astrid both sit in hold-up positions and will look to pounce from the back third, while Electric Arc's tendency to fade late makes her role passive. This race shape — a single unchallenged leader setting a fair but unspectacular tempo over an extended trip — classically favours patient, mid-to-rear runners who get a clean run around the home turn, tilting the tactical verdict firmly in favour of the hold-up profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone leader controls race
scenarios.trigger: If Affettuoso dictates an uncontested, measured pace throughout, the tempo remains fair but not burning.
scenarios.body: Affettuoso bowls along in front without pressure, leaving hold-up horses needing an exceptional turn of foot around the home bend to reel her in; horses tracking the pace from midfield are best placed to deliver that challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses pounce late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady enough to compress the field and hold-up runners find a clear passage turning for home.
scenarios.body: Oneinthewell and Astrid, sitting patiently off the single leader, get the run of the race around Lingfield's long left-hand bend and produce late surges that overhaul a front-runner who has done too much early work.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapses, winner emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Affettuoso goes too hard early and ties up inside the final two furlongs, inviting a late finishing effort.
scenarios.body: A fading Affettuoso is swallowed up by closers who have conserved energy in a truly-run race that turns into a stamina examination over the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent runner outstays field
scenarios.trigger: If Lost In Wonder tracks Affettuoso closely and benefits from a steady pace that never quickens sufficiently to worry front two.
scenarios.body: Lost In Wonder, racing just off Affettuoso's shoulder throughout, picks up the pieces if the hold-up horses fail to find a clear run around the home turn; her prominent position proves decisive in a race run at a false pace.

watchPoints.text: Oneinthewell's going concern is real — all her form is on turf Good/Soft over marathon trips, and if the Standard Polytrack surface blunts her finishing effort she may never land a blow despite a favourable pace scenario.
Affettuoso's 95-day layoff means fitness is unproven; if Roger Varian's filly ties up after two furlongs of solo work, the race unravels quickly for any backers expecting front-running dominance.

Electric Arc is flagged as fading in the finish and arrives on a 138-day absence with only one AW run behind her — watch for her being pulled up or weakening markedly from two furlongs out if the pace has any bite.

With all five draws rated NEUTRAL and the course layout favouring middle-path racing on the Polytrack, early positioning out of the gate matters less than which horse can secure a clear, wide run around Lingfield's final sweeping bend — watch for traffic problems among the hold-up trio in the straight.

runners_data.name: James Choice
runners_data.note: Stepping up to 1m4f having placed at 12f and 11f on Standard going, the form arc is pointing upward and Warren Greatrex's yard is finding winners at a functional 1/14 clip; midfield style suits a scenario where the prominent group churns each other out and he can pick up the pieces.|

runners_data.name: Hebridean Nomad
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's five-year-old has placed six times in eight Standard-going starts including a course-and-distance win, and arrives with back-to-back 13f AW placed efforts confirming he handles this exact trip; prominent style at a draw of 10 should allow a clean run into the race without being boxed in by the inner congestion.|

runners_data.name: Captain Fox
runners_data.note: Won on his sole outing at 8f on Standard but steps up notably in trip to 1m4f here, and the form book shows sprint-to-mile distances until today; prominent style from stall 1 is tactically interesting on the inside rail, though whether he truly stays is the core uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Bankatary
runners_data.note: Consistent form figures (4-5-6) on Standard going over 10-12f provide a reasonable baseline, but has yet to place on this surface and carries the highest weight at 142lbs which could blunt his finish when the race quickens; prominent intent from stall 8 means he will need a quick early break to slot in without burning energy.|

runners_data.name: Zarco
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's three-year-old has run consistently in the 4-6 range but all form is on Good or Soft turf, making this AW debut a genuine query; he is a natural prominent racer whose position has been mapped to midfield in the pace distribution because the field is saturated with forward-going types, meaning he is unlikely to operate at his preferred pitch and that style friction tempers expectations.|

runners_data.name: Pace Attack
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's hold-up runner won over 11f on Standard just 12 days ago and is the freshest improver in the field; Luke Morris can ride cold and find late gaps, and the horse's hood worn previously suggests a switched-off demeanour that suits waiting tactics — the chief danger if traffic allows a clean passage.|

runners_data.name: Rossa Raheen
runners_data.note: Has no AW form on record and all five runs have come on Good or Soft turf, which is a material surface concern on Polytrack here; showed enough to win a 12f turf handicap so the trip is not in doubt, but the surface question means he needs everything to go right and carries genuine going-fit risk.|

runners_data.name: White Storm
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field — visor worn, capable of dictating from the outside draw at stall 9, and placed over 11f on Standard going; the single-pace scenario is his ally, and if the prominent pack decides to track rather than chase he could steal margins the closers simply cannot recover.|

runners_data.name: Affection
runners_data.note: David Pipe's three-year-old placed at 12f on Standard going and has form at a variety of trip lengths including 17f on Good, so stamina is not a concern; prominent style and a middle draw at stall 4 gives a clean position inside the field, and Ashley Lewis's 3lb claim makes the weight look attractive if the horse fires.|

runners_data.name: Wise Counsellor
runners_data.note: All form on record is over much longer trips on Good going — as far as 19f — and the step back to 1m4f on Polytrack is an abrupt change of context; a hold-up type by label but the stayers' form profile suggests grinding rather than finishing speed, and without AW experience the horse is difficult to evaluate confidently here.|

races.paceDynamic: White Storm is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m4f Polytrack trip. Behind him, a cluster of prominent types — Hebridean Nomad, Captain Fox, Bankatary, Affection, and the redistributed Zarco — will compete for the handful of positions just off the pace, creating a likely squeeze and potential shuffling through the first half-mile as horses jostle for berth. This congestion 2-3 furlongs out is the key tactical risk: runners caught wide or blocked in traffic could find their challenge blunted at the critical moment. The field holds more prominent-running types than can all secure their natural position, with Hebridean Nomad and Affection — better credentialled on this surface and trip — most likely to actually land the prominent slots ahead of the rest. A single, unhurried pace set by White Storm with a compacted chasing group behind him is the dominant shape, and it strongly favours horses who can sit prominently in a well-organised position and deliver a sustained finishing effort rather than a sharp late sprint — making prominent hold-position types the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If White Storm sets an uncontested, even gallop and the prominent group settles cleanly behind him.
scenarios.body: White Storm's lone lead creates a fair but not slow pace, allowing the prominent horses to conserve energy through the middle stages and mount sustained challenges from 2f out; Hebridean Nomad, with strong recent form at this course and trip on Standard going, is ideally placed to travel into the race and wear down any rival. Affection and Captain Fox, if they can secure clean prominent berths without being squeezed, also profile well for this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Trouble Assists Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group creates sustained interference and hold-up horses find a clear passage late.
scenarios.body: The congestion among five prominent types materialises into lasting interference, negating the positional advantages and leaving the race open to late closers who thread through on the rail or outer; Pace Attack, a winner over 11f on Standard going with a hold-up tag, is the standout beneficiary with Luke Morris able to find gaps. Wise Counsellor has struggled for form but the step back to a more competitive pace with a clear run could sharpen him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: White Storm Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that White Storm is never seriously challenged and wins from the front.
scenarios.body: An unusually sedate early gallop — possible if the prominent pack opts to track rather than press — hands White Storm an unassailable lead turning for home, and with a visor on and front-running form over 11f on Standard he has the tactical kit to exploit it. None of the hold-up types would generate enough late pace in a truly dawdling affair to reel him in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble, Longshot Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group over-races early fighting for position and collectively ties up in the straight.
scenarios.body: An overcooked early tempo caused by multiple horses surging for the same berths drains the prominent contingent, opening the door for a horse on the outer or improving through beaten rivals; Rossa Raheen carries an AW-form concern but showed turf form over this trip and could capitalise if the pace implodes. James Choice, stepping up to 1m4f with upward-trending form figures, is another to consider if pace collapses.

watchPoints.text: Prominent traffic squeeze — with Hebridean Nomad, Captain Fox, Bankatary, Affection, and Zarco all wanting the chasing positions behind White Storm, watch for early bumping and jostling from stalls 1-10 that could unsettle any one of them and effectively remove a market contender from the race before 3f is covered.

Zarco's AW debut combined with a style mismatch — pushed back to midfield from his natural prominent pitch — means Pat Cosgrave may find himself in no-man's land through the first mile, neither dictating nor holding up, which could produce a flat, inconclusive effort.

Rossa Raheen has flagged going concern with zero AW form; if the Polytrack surface rides quicker than his turf experience suits, Charles Bishop may find the horse failing to travel in his usual manner and dropping out of contention earlier than his RPR suggests.

White Storm's lone front-running role from stall 9 is only advantageous if he can cross cleanly to his preferred position without being pressed — Captain Fox from stall 1 could push out and contest the rail, forcing White Storm to exert energy earlier than ideal if Richard Hughes has instructed a forward pitch.

Pace Attack's rapid return (12 days) is worth tracking in the preliminaries; Sir Mark Prescott horses are reliably fit when produced quickly, but monitor the pre-race demeanour given the hood record — if he is fractious at the start his hold-up tactics could be compromised before a stride is taken.

runners_data.name: Amber Honey
runners_data.note: Pat Phelan's 4yo has a 12/15 similar-going record suggesting course-surface compatibility, but her natural instinct is to race from the back — in a field already overloaded with hold-up horses she'll likely find herself unable to get cover and will be racing in an unnatural position throughout; discount her chances unless the pace blows up.

runners_data.name: Borderline Madness
runners_data.note: William Stone runner arrives on 28 days' rest with headgear (p) and a solid similar-going mark of 6/8; his one win in this form string (1/8f/STA) came over this exact trip on this surface and he's the most respected midfield threat if the field strings out late.

runners_data.name: Berning Hot
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater's yard is firing (T14: 1/13) and Alistair Rawlinson takes the ride on a horse whose 2/8f/STA effort hints at 1m AW aptitude; however, Berning Hot's hold-up style will need something to go wrong up front — a passive pace gives him little to close onto.

runners_data.name: Mount Mogan
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran for Laura Mongan who carries a fade-in-finish flag from recent data, but his defining advantage today is sole front-runner status — with nobody to pressure him, Luke Morris can regulate every fraction and the fade risk is mitigated by controlling the tempo himself.

runners_data.name: Chico Dulce
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's principal danger, George Wood aboard, with 8/8 on similar going — this horse handles the surface thoroughly and races from behind, which in a steady-pace scenario is a minor drawback, but his consistency (never far away, 1W3P in sim-going) means he must be respected as the most likely closer to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Victory Sound
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard's top pick (low confidence flagged) for Mark Usher — Connor Beasley takes over on a horse showing sharp recent form (621 in last three) on this surface; crucially, his true hold-up style means he's mapped forward only due to field composition, and his actual position will be rear-to-midfield, making the task harder in a steady-pace race.

runners_data.name: Turpin
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle has the yard in decent order (T14: 2/21) and Pat Cosgrave is an experienced Lingfield pilot; Turpin's prominent style suits the race shape well and his 3/8f/STA effort shows he can hit the frame on this surface, making him a logical second-string beneficiary if Mount Mogan ties up.

runners_data.name: Taskheer
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old for Gary & Josh Moore wearing a tongue-tie and boasting 8/8 similar-going exposure — strong surface familiarity but a career 0 wins from 5 in this recent run of form suggests he finishes in the money without quite getting there; his prominent style is an asset today.

runners_data.name: Muy Muy Loco
runners_data.note: Simon Dow has been active (T14: 3/13) and Harry Davies rides this 4yo who wears hood (h) — the 1/10f/STA win suggests he needs longer trips to show his best and the 1m distance is shorter than his recent comfort zone; his hold-up style and trip concern combine to make this a tough ask.

races.paceDynamic: Mount Mogan (draw 5, prominent style) is the lone confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and will likely dictate from the front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop — a significant tactical advantage on Lingfield's flat Polytrack mile. Turpin and Taskheer will push forward from their draws to press for prominent positions directly behind, creating a steady rather than scorching pace that could allow Mount Mogan to control margins into the straight. The redistribution note is important: Victory Sound and Amber Honey are genuine hold-up horses mapped forward on the pace map only because the field contains more closers than the rear of the map can accommodate — both are likely to race further back than their mapped position suggests, meaning true late pace may be thinner than it appears. This shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a measured tempo — most favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can sit just off the pace, travel comfortably, and produce a sustained challenge rather than a sharp late burst; deep hold-up horses will likely find the steady gallop insufficient to generate the gap they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mogan Controls, Stays Clean
scenarios.trigger: If Mount Mogan is allowed to dictate an uncontested, metronomic gallop and turns for home with daylight.
scenarios.body: Mount Mogan leads without a fight, sets a pace that suits his stamina profile, and the finish becomes a test of who has travelled best — prominently-raced horses who have conserved energy get first run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chase Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners close behind Mount Mogan travels smoothly and pounces inside the final furlong as the leader ties up.
scenarios.body: Turpin or Taskheer sit second or third in a carbon-copy position throughout, find the winner weakening late, and muster a decisive challenge; the lack of early pressure means they arrive fresh.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely slow enough to produce a sprint finish and a horse travelling powerfully from mid-division arrives with a decisive late run.
scenarios.body: A compressed field in the straight creates a scrimmage where a horse switching out and finishing strongly can pick off tired rivals; Borderline Madness and Chico Dulce have the style to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo quickens sharply mid-race and creates genuine late ground for the genuine hold-up horses who find their natural position at the rear.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because Victory Sound and Amber Honey are redistributed from the rear and unlikely to secure their natural late-running berth; only if the pace blows up does a true closer get into it.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Turpin or Taskheer push forward aggressively to sit second and third behind Mount Mogan — if either secures that position they become the primary threat to overhaul the leader inside the final furlong.

Monitor Mount Mogan's sectionals in the first two furlongs; if Luke Morris is allowed to coast unchallenged and sets a crawling pace, the whole field will bunch turning in and the prominent advantage largely evaporates.

Victory Sound (Strand Scorecard top pick) carries a style-fit discount — if Connor Beasley is forced wide or finds no cover from draw 1, the horse's natural hold-up game may be compromised before a ball is bowled.

Chico Dulce's 8/8 similar-going record is the strongest surface reliability figure in the field — if anything disrupts the front two in the straight, he is the most likely horse to arrive late and capitalise.

Berning Hot and Amber Honey are the two purest closers likely to race genuinely last — in a slow-pace scenario their finishing kicks may not be enough, but they represent each-way insurance if the race falls apart for the leaders.

runners_data.name: Yazoo
runners_data.note: Proven front-runner who has won over 8f on Standard AW, holds a course-form angle, and from stall 3 should find the rail early; the STYLE_FIT tag is a mild caution given the rating of 54, but the pace map clearly revolves around him — his chance is real.

runners_data.name: Aurelune
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley takes the ride on this Richard & Peter Fahey-trained filly with solid placed form over 8f on both soft and standard ground; a genuine midfield type who has hit the frame twice at the trip and is drawn favourably in stall 2, though her win rate is zero.

runners_data.name: Melodical
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's charge has consistent placed form on Standard AW and grass over sprint-to-mile trips; midfield in style and sensibly drawn in stall 5, she should travel comfortably into the straight but has yet to win in five starts.

runners_data.name: Cortado Girl
runners_data.note: A prominent-style filly returning from a 72-day break for a small trainer with a flat 14-day strike rate; limited form in just two starts and drawn in stall 4 — the layoff combined with modest formlines makes her a speculative factor at best.

runners_data.name: Creciente
runners_data.note: Carries a genuine AW going concern flag with no Polytrack or Tapeta experience, having run exclusively on grass; has useful form including a 7f win and a second on Good, but the surface unknown is a significant risk to her hold-up style on this card.

runners_data.name: Henfield
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's leading danger, with three recent 1m AW starts reading 1-2-4 and a wearers-of-the-visor headgear note suggesting he switches on for the contest; Luke Morris takes the ride from the wide stall 10, which is neutral at Lingfield 1m but will require a clean early move to secure his prominent position.

runners_data.name: Ernie McCrew
runners_data.note: J S Moore's horse has run seven times on Standard AW over 8f and has finished in the frame twice, showing consistency without winning; prominent in style from stall 7, he is the type to pop up at a price if Yazoo's pace creates an opportunity but the overall profile is limited.

runners_data.name: Poetic Grace
runners_data.note: A genuine front-running type by nature — Conrad Allen's filly has run prominently in all recent starts — but the field is too packed with prominent horses for her to secure that role from the wide stall 8, so she is mapped to midfield; her best odds-on scenario is a contested early pace that suits a late run she may not naturally possess.

runners_data.name: Mokata
runners_data.note: No AW form to speak of and a 74-day absence for Adam Kirby's stable, which has a flat recent strike rate; the tp headgear could spark interest, but the combination of an unknown surface and a long layoff makes this a very speculative hold-up runner.

runners_data.name: Irish Fusilier
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's runner has only one start on Standard going out of five recent runs, finishing last over 7f; steps up to a mile which is uncharted territory, and the form string shows little encouragement — his midfield style needs a higher-class platform to deliver.

races.paceDynamic: Yazoo is the sole confirmed front-runner and, breaking from stall 3, should find the lead comfortably without any genuine challengers for that position — Cortado Girl and Ernie McCrew have prominent tendencies but neither has the early zip to overhaul a horse with a proven front-running profile. With Yazoo setting a controlled, sustainable gallop on Standard Polytrack over 1m, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which historically at Lingfield AW benefits horses who can sit just behind the leader and pounce off the turn. The field holds more prominent-style runners than can all secure their favoured position: Poetic Grace and Henfield are genuine prominent types but, with Yazoo commanding the rail and Cortado Girl and Ernie McCrew also pressing forward, one or more of them will find themselves shuffled wider or further back than ideal. This race shape — a single leader setting a measured tempo — most favours hold-up and late-closing profiles who can exploit the bunching in the straight, provided they have the class to quicken on the Polytrack surface.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Yazoo Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Yazoo leads unchallenged and sets a controlled tempo that denies closers a strong enough early pace to reel him in.
scenarios.body: Yazoo dictates from the front at a comfortable gallop and, with no rival willing or able to press him hard through the middle sector, retains enough energy to repel challengers in the Lingfield straight; prominent types who sat just off him, such as Henfield or Ernie McCrew, are best placed to chase him home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfielders Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough in the early stages to drain front-runners, allowing midfield runners to pick up strongly off the home turn.
scenarios.body: Aurelune or Melodical, sitting comfortably in the middle of the field, travel well into the straight and power past a tiring Yazoo; Standard Polytrack at Lingfield rewards those with a clean run from mid-division when the leader has had a solo gallop but not a dawdling one.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and front-runners hit the two-furlong marker with little left in reserve.
scenarios.body: Creciente or Mokata, dropping back from their grass form into an AW context for the first time, attempt to produce a late run from off the pace — but both carry significant AW form concerns and Creciente's going flag must temper expectations even if the shape theoretically suits.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners contest the early lead, fracturing the race shape and causing a contested, messy pace that benefits whoever gets a clear run soonest.
scenarios.body: With Cortado Girl, Ernie McCrew and Poetic Grace all pressing from outside draws, a brief scrimmage for position could unsettle Yazoo's rhythm, leaving a prominent racer who finds daylight early — most likely Henfield wide in stall 10 — to steal a march on rivals who are stuck behind traffic.

watchPoints.text: Henfield (stall 10) needs to move across promptly from the wide draw to secure a prominent pitch behind Yazoo — if Luke Morris gets caught wide and fails to slot in, his chance diminishes significantly.
Creciente and Mokata both carry NO AW FORM flags on Standard Polytrack; if either underperforms early due to surface unfamiliarity, they will not be competitive regardless of the pace shape.

Poetic Grace is a natural front-runner who cannot get her preferred position with Yazoo, Cortado Girl and Ernie McCrew all pressing forward — watch whether Alice Bond (5) elects to restrain her or burn petrol fighting for ground she is unlikely to secure.

Yazoo's lead is only valuable if it is unhurried — if Cortado Girl from stall 4 pushes forward aggressively in the early stages and forces Yazoo to quicken earlier than ideal, the front-runner's stamina reserves could be compromised by the final furlong.

Aurelune in stall 2 is the hidden draw beneficiary — a clean break could allow Connor Beasley to slot in just off Yazoo's shoulder on the inside rail, giving her the most economical route through the race of all the midfield runners.

runners_data.name: Tatterstall
runners_data.note: All his recent form is on good ground, making the Polytrack surface a legitimate query; drawn 6 in a neutral spot, he wants to race prominently but will need to hold position in a congested early phase without his ideal going underfoot.

runners_data.name: Kylian
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's runner has AW experience (two Standard-going runs) but has not troubled the judge on that surface (best sim-going finish: 3rd); a natural front-end racer whose chance is meaningfully compromised by the abundance of pace in this field, pushing him into a midfield role that does not suit his 0.95 style-fit score.

runners_data.name: Layla Liz
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's filly has a compelling AW record — one win from three starts on Standard going — and her 84-day absence is the main concern; drawn 4 on the inside of the prominent pack, she has genuine claims if returnng to her course-winning form.

runners_data.name: Spartan Arrow
runners_data.note: Topped the Strand Scorecard at high confidence; drawn 7 in a viable middle position, he is proven on Standard Polytrack (one win from six sim-going runs) and Watson's yard is in strong form (T14: 4/19), though a string of 7s and 8s in recent form suggests he needs things to drop right.

runners_data.name: Law Of Average
runners_data.note: Multiple winner on exactly this surface and distance (-11314 form), she is the chief pace-setter and her freshness after 57 days adds intrigue; Banham's yard is quiet (T14: 0/2) but this mare has the track record to compensate for trainer stats and could easily control from the front.

runners_data.name: Our Cody
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with no AW experience at all — a concern on Polytrack — and his natural style is prominent rather than the hold-up role the redistribution assigns; Richard Hughes' runner carries a STYLE_FIT discount (0.88) and the surface unknown keeps the risk high.

runners_data.name: Regal Envoy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old drawn on the inside rail at stall 2, he wants to lead but will have to assert immediately against Law Of Average and Solar Edge; his Standard-going form shows no wins or places from two runs (sim-going: 0W0P), which undermines his claims if the pace war dulls his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Dandana
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's three-year-old has no AW form and all her recent runs have been over 6f on turf — stepping back to 5f on Polytrack is a double unknown; her best effort (2nd at Goodwood) came over 6f on good ground, which doesn't obviously translate here.

runners_data.name: Michaela's Boy
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's second string won over 5f on good going (GOO) and has one AW win in his record, but his Standard-going return is limited (7 runs, 1W2P); pushed toward the rear by the redistribution despite being a prominent type — STYLE_FIT 0.87 — he would need significant early chaos to benefit.

runners_data.name: Solar Edge
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 5f on good ground and has shown versatility (two wins: one on AW FIR, one on GOO); drawn 5 in a mid-low stall and will try to lead alongside Law Of Average and Regal Envoy, but three-way pace arguments at 5f on a flat track rarely end well for all parties.

races.paceDynamic: Law Of Average, Regal Envoy, and Solar Edge all want to lead from the front in a 5f Lingfield sprint, guaranteeing a genuinely strong early gallop with three horses fighting for supremacy from the gates. This contested pace will string the field out early, burning off prominent types like Tatterstall, Layla Liz, Spartan Arrow, and Dandana who must try to slot in behind a wall of speed, creating significant positional congestion 2-3 furlongs out. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate — Kylian and Michaela's Boy, both natural prominent racers, are effectively squeezed into rear positions they would not naturally choose, meaning their redistribution genuinely compromises their effectiveness. A strong, even gallop on a flat Polytrack surface at this trip historically favours horses who can travel just off a genuine pace and sustain their effort through the closing stages — the sweet spot here is a horse with tactical speed to sit second or third early without burning energy, giving Spartan Arrow and Layla Liz the ideal profile to pounce.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Suits Stalkers
scenarios.trigger: If Law Of Average, Regal Envoy, and Solar Edge set a truly fierce early pace and burn each other out by halfway.
scenarios.body: The three leaders fight for supremacy and set a punishing gallop that leaves them vulnerable entering the final furlong, gifting the patient prominent horses a straightforward run to the line. Spartan Arrow, travelling just off the speed, and Layla Liz, proven on this surface, are best placed to pick up the pieces as the pace dissolves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Defies Hot Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front runners — most likely Law Of Average — breaks cleanly and secures a crucial half-length advantage to dictate from a controlled position.
scenarios.body: Law Of Average, proven course and distance winner with multiple wins on similar surfaces, has the class to take back the pace just enough to control the race from the front and hold on. With a 57-day break freshening her up and strong course form (-11314), she has every chance of fronting up to win.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Congestion Punishes Prominents
scenarios.trigger: If the early scrimmaging causes serious interference 2-3 furlongs out, blocking off the prominent horses and leaving the field strung along the rail.
scenarios.body: Horses redistributed to the rear like Michaela's Boy, a genuine prominent type forced wide or back, could get a clear run through in the straight with little to beat ahead; however the STYLE_FIT discount (0.87) tempers this materially. Dandana, despite no AW form, could benefit if the scrimmage opens a passage through the centre.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so strong that the entire prominent group is compromised and a horse from the rear delivers a sustained finish down the straight.
scenarios.body: This shape relies on Our Cody or Kylian — both redistributed from their natural prominent role — delivering a hold-up performance they are not naturally suited to, making this scenario inherently unlikely. Only a truly exceptional pace meltdown would create enough daylight for this profile to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Law Of Average and Regal Envoy are both drawn inside Solar Edge (stalls 8 and 2 vs 5) — watch for a three-horse battle for lead position in the opening furlong that could create early crossing and interference for the prominent horses tracking them.

Spartan Arrow (stall 7) and Layla Liz (stall 4) are separated by the width of the field at the start — watch whether either gets blocked by the pace war developing inside them, as a clean early position is critical to their chance in this scenario.

Kylian (stall 9) is a natural front-end horse forced into mid-pack — watch for him making an unexpected early move to try and reclaim his natural position, which could cause interference to Tatterstall (stall 6) and Spartan Arrow directly around him.

Our Cody (stall 10, outermost) has no AW experience at all — watch for early signs of unsettled behaviour or unfamiliarity with the Polytrack kickback, which could neutralise him before the race reaches its critical phase.

Dandana's headgear note (tongue tie) and step down from 6f on turf to 5f AW is a surface-and-trip combination she has never faced — watch the market moves for any market confidence that Crisford's team believe she handles the surface.

races.paceDynamic: Quick Quasar and Pennine Way are the two confirmed front-runners and will battle for the lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than a dawdle — on Standard Polytrack at Lingfield over 7f this is likely to produce an honest, true-run race from the off. The prominent group is crowded: Angels' Share, Tie Fighter, Venetian Romance, and Orange Emperor all want to race close to the pace, meaning there will be congestion and potential traffic trouble 2-3f out as positions are negotiated around the home turn. Mr Jeffrey is a genuine hold-up type whose natural position has been displaced by the sheer weight of pace and prominent horses in this field — in practice, the rear of the field will be less populous with true closers than the draw suggests, meaning late-running scenarios depend on horses that are not natural hold-up operators. This race shape — a genuine pace duel up front with a packed prominent group — classically favours a relaxed, well-positioned prominent or midfield horse with tactical pace to pick off the tiring leaders entering the straight, rather than either the pace-setters who risk burning out or deep closers who may find insufficient daylight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Horse Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Quick Quasar and Pennine Way fight it out at the head of affairs and set a genuine gallop that softens both, a prominent racer tracking just off the pace pounces in the straight.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners push each other along through the first half, leaving the prominent stalkers ideally placed rounding the home turn with energy to spare; the 7f trip and Standard surface at Lingfield rewards exactly this profile of horse who has settled and quickened.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Quick Quasar — asserts early dominance and Pennine Way fails to sustain the duel, allowing a controlled lead through the middle stages.
scenarios.body: Quick Quasar's natural front-running style combined with Luke Morris's experience of AW tracks could allow a slide into a comfortable rhythm once Pennine Way drops away; from that position in a truly-run race a brave front-runner can hold on if the prominent group don't coordinate their challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Raids Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel is scorching enough to set up the race for a genuine late finisher finding a clear passage in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Dance Fantasy, who has form on this track and surface, is the most credible late-finishing type in the field; the congestion in the prominent group could create openings on the outside for a horse ridden quietly from off the pace, though the field volume makes a clean run far from guaranteed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group of four gets into a physical battle for position 3f out, causing interference and opening a route for a lower-rated runner to sneak through.
scenarios.body: Carnage in the prominent pack around the home turn could momentarily disrupt the fancied horses, giving a lower-rated type that has been quietly tracking outside the melee a fortuitous opening; this is the chaos scenario and requires multiple horses to traffic-check each other.

watchPoints.text: Quick Quasar and Pennine Way — watch the first furlong closely: if Pennine Way pushes Quick Quasar into a flat-out duel before the 6f marker, both could be spent before the straight and the scenario shifts sharply to Scenario A.

Angels' Share — if Taylor Fisher tracks the leaders from stall 9 and finds herself boxed behind the prominent group on the home turn, a winner's chance evaporates; watch for whether she gets a clear sight of the rail approaching 2f out.

Orange Emperor — drawn in stall 3 with prominent horses on both sides, Ashley Lewis (3) needs to slot in cleanly and avoid getting shuffled back; the horse's tendency to race wide on the AW is a traffic concern with four prominent types fighting for position.

Dance Fantasy — the 194-day absence makes the early market move (if any) highly informative; Harry Davies is a capable conditional and if the Crisford yard has this primed, a late run from the hold-up berth is viable, but watch for signs of ring-rustiness in the pre-race.

Venetian Romance — the hood is noted and the surface switch from Good to Standard AW is a live unknown; if she breaks smartly from stall 6 and travels easily in the prominent group she is one to monitor, but any sign of reluctance on the surface and she can be discounted quickly.

races.paceDynamic: Vitality (draw 2) and Credit Forgedd It (draw 6) are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over 7f on Standard Polytrack, manufacturing an honest, competitive gallop rather than a dawdle. Behind them, Strong Voice, Royal County Glory, Green Testimony, and Bessie Wallis all want prominent positions, creating a congested pocket 2-3 furlongs out where traffic disruption is a genuine risk for those unable to secure their natural berth early. Harlequin Bay is a genuine prominent type but is mapped to midfield because the field simply cannot accommodate five horses in the first two lengths — expect it to be shuffled back against its will and to race out of its most effective role. This race shape — honest pace set by two genuine leaders, with a traffic-heavy mid-race — most favours a horse that can track just off the pace in a clean position without burning energy fighting for it, meaning a well-drawn, well-grounded prominent runner with Lingfield AW course form is the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Vitality and Credit Forgedd It set a genuine honest gallop and a prominent horse tracks smoothly into contention without traffic trouble from 2f out.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners churn out even splits, stringing the field out and eliminating any tactical sprint finish; the horse who has raced prominently in a clean position simply picks them off approaching the furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Vitality or Credit Forgedd It — gets a soft lead and the contested gallop paradoxically becomes one-sided as the other capitulates.
scenarios.body: With the early pace fight resolved in favour of one leader, that horse settles into a rhythm, conserves enough energy to resist the challenge, and the hold-up brigade cannot reel it in over 7f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Late Swooper
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion mid-race causes significant interference and bunching 3f out, creating a wall that blocks most of the field.
scenarios.body: Honky Tonk Girl or Real Gold, racing from hold-up positions outside the traffic, finds daylight late on the rising Lingfield finish and gobbles up beaten rivals who burned energy fighting for position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Lands
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners burn each other out badly and decelerate sharply in the final 2f, leaving a vacuum that rewards the deepest closers.
scenarios.body: Real Gold or Honky Tonk Girl, having settled furthest back and conserved maximum energy, relentlessly closes the gap as the leaders tie up; however, this depends on a degree of pace collapse that Standard AW conditions rarely produce at Lingfield.

watchPoints.text: Royal County Glory (draw 4) must secure a clean prominent position early — if it gets squeezed between Vitality and Credit Forgedd It fighting for the rail, its chance is compromised before the race properly begins.

Credit Forgedd It (draw 6) and Vitality (draw 2) both break keenly; watch the first furlong for one capitulating — if either backs off, the other could get a cheap lead and the race shape shifts sharply toward Scenario B.

Harlequin Bay will likely be unable to hold its natural prominent position given the prominent congestion — watch whether Pat Cosgrave accepts midfield or fights for position, as the latter wastes energy and worsens its chance further.

Green Testimony's 157-day absence is the key unknown — watch it in the pre-parade ring and early in the race for any sign of ring-rustiness or an over-fresh break, which would either help (jumping prominently) or hurt (boiling over) its chance.

The prominent cluster of Strong Voice, Royal County Glory, Bessie Wallis, and Green Testimony creates a genuine traffic risk 2-3f out — any runner caught in that pocket faces a significant momentum check on the turn into the straight.

races.paceDynamic: Buckland Belle is the lone confirmed front-runner and, drawn in stall 2 on a flat Lingfield AW mile, she is likely to stride into an uncontested lead from the outset with Luke Morris able to dictate entirely on her own terms. Espanita and Kaori are both prominent types who will pressure the early positions, but with Sunshine And Roses also a natural prominent racer who cannot realistically secure her preferred spot given the congestion up front, she is effectively pushed back into midfield — meaning the pace picture ahead is led by Buckland Belle with Espanita and Kaori tracking closely. This creates a genuine, sustainable gallop rather than a dawdle, which on Standard Polytrack over a mile is likely to produce a true-run race where stamina and cruising efficiency are rewarded over sprint finish. Front-runners and close-prominent stalkers who can travel within the pace without expending energy early are best placed; hold-up types like Lili Marleen face an uphill task from well off a true pace on this surface, and the field holds more prominent types than can all occupy their preferred ground, with Buckland Belle and Espanita most likely to actually secure their natural positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Belle Controls, Stalkers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Buckland Belle dictates an honest but not suicidal gallop and the prominent stalkers track within two lengths throughout.
scenarios.body: Buckland Belle sets a metronomic pace that stretches the hold-up horses while Espanita and Kaori track in her wake ready to challenge from two furlongs out; horses who travel prominently without burning fuel early dominate the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalkers Overhaul Leader Late
scenarios.trigger: If Buckland Belle's lead is whittled down in the straight and a tracking racer quickens past her.
scenarios.body: Espanita, who boasts strong AW form with two wins and four places from ten similar-going starts, is ideally positioned to pounce; Kaori's hat-trick of placed efforts at this trip and course style also makes her a live threat in a strong-staying finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lovers Leap Surprises From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than expected and Lovers Leap, dropping back to AW for the first time, finds the surface suiting her sharp turn of foot from midfield.
scenarios.body: Jane Chapple-Hyam's filly showed progressive form on Goodwood turf including a win, and a true gallop could play to her late momentum if she handles the Polytrack surface; the AW concern flag is real, but 28 days fresh and a genuine pace to run at gives her the best possible scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race collapses into an unexpected sprint finish and a closer can make ground from the back.
scenarios.body: Lili Marleen has shown no meaningful form across five recent AW starts and Sunshine And Roses, though a natural prominent racer shuffled back by the field's pace profile, lacks the hold-up credentials to execute a true late run; this scenario is unlikely given the confirmed honest pace set by Buckland Belle.

watchPoints.text: Buckland Belle's front-running advantage is real but her seven similar-going AW runs have produced zero wins — if she fails to convert from the front again, the Strand Scorecard's low-confidence flag will prove prescient and Espanita's superior AW strike-rate becomes decisive.

Lovers Leap has no AW form whatsoever and Polytrack can be unforgiving for turf specialists on debut on the surface — watch how she travels in the first three furlongs to gauge whether she acclimatises.

Sunshine And Roses is a natural prominent racer who is likely to be outgunned for early position by Buckland Belle, Espanita, and Kaori — if she is forced to race further back than comfortable, her chance is materially compromised regardless of her recent placed AW form.

Post Rider returns just two days after her last run — monitor the market for signs this sharp turnaround is intentional and supported, as trainer Oliver Cole's 2-from-10 14-day strike rate is modest and quick returns can signal either freshness or necessity.

races.paceDynamic: Walking On Clouds is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with a draw in stall 9, will stride across to lead from the outset with Joey Haynes able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop — this horse has won twice on Lingfield AW at this trip and knows exactly how to exploit a clear lead. The prominent pack is congested: Kyoto, Mart, Alashos, and the redistributed Magic Lady Mae and Iconic Dawn all want to race close to the pace, meaning a scramble for the first three positions is inevitable in the opening furlong, creating traffic friction 2-3f out rather than a pressured early pace. That congestion is more likely to hinder the chasers than to unsettle Walking On Clouds, who should settle into a rhythm on a soft lead and put rivals in a flat-out chase from the 2f pole. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure that position — Alashos, with a low draw in stall 1, and Kyoto are best placed to physically hold prominent ground; Magic Lady Mae and Iconic Dawn are likely to be shuffled into mid-division against their instincts. This race shape strongly favours a front-runner who controls tempo and has course-proven stamina for the straight finish — the dominant tactical profile here is lead-and-sustain.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Wins Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Walking On Clouds jumps cleanly and is allowed an uncontested lead through the first two furlongs, settling into its rhythm while the prominent pack scraps behind.
scenarios.body: Walking On Clouds dictates a comfortable gallop, conserves energy through the turn, and has enough in reserve to repel challengers in the straight — its 2W2P record on Lingfield AW at 6f in standard conditions is the decisive evidence.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poacher Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Walking On Clouds is matched for early pace and the lead is softer than anticipated, allowing a prominent horse to pounce in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Alashos, drawn widest in stall 1 on the inside, can track Walking On Clouds throughout and mount a sustained challenge from 2f out if the leader ties up even fractionally — Alashos has won at this course and distance in standard going.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage creates a fast enough early pace to stop Walking On Clouds, leaving late ground for hold-up runners to close.
scenarios.body: Henry Tudor or Rianka, racing from the rear without traffic issues, could pick up the pieces if the lead group tie each other up in the final furlong — however, neither has strong AW form at this course, limiting confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Walking On Clouds is pressured from multiple prominent rivals early and the whole field races keenly, collapsing the pace and handing the race to a fresh-legged outsider.
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly hot pace could see Mayfair Market or Mart, both capable of racing prominently and finishing, benefit as the race blows up in front of them — a low-probability shape given the clear pace hierarchy but not impossible given Mart's 2-day turnaround.

watchPoints.text: Walking On Clouds (stall 9) must cross quickly to the rail and establish the lead unchallenged — watch the first furlong for any rival matching her stride, as even a modest early duel could significantly change the race shape.

Alashos (stall 1) has the ideal low draw to sit second and track the leader throughout — watch whether Charles Bishop elects to shadow Walking On Clouds from the outset, as that is the one move most likely to produce a challenger in the straight.

The prominent group (Kyoto, Mart, Magic Lady Mae, Iconic Dawn) all want to race forward from varied draws — potential for interference and checking between stalls 5-10 in the first furlong, which could unsettle any runner drawn in that cluster.

Mart ran just two days ago; watch for early signs of staleness or sluggishness at the start, particularly as a horse who likes to race close to the pace — if he misses the break, his chance is essentially gone.

Exhibitioning is flagged as a fader and carries top weight at OR 60 from stall 7 — watch the 2f-out mark for whether she drops out sharply, as that could create a pocket or gap for any hold-up runner tracking her.
